q: Will Brazil's regulated carbon market let pig iron and steel exporters reduce CBAM costs?
title: Brazil's carbon market and CBAM
short: Only once a carbon price is actually paid. Brazil's law creating its emissions trading system phases it in over several years, starting with reporting before any allowance cost. Until a producer pays for its emissions, there is nothing for the EU declarant to deduct.
audience: Brazilian steel, pig iron and aluminium exporters and their EU declarants

p: Article 9 of the CBAM Regulation lets the declarant deduct the carbon price effectively paid in the country of origin for the embedded emissions, after free allocation and any rebate.

ul: Start the monitoring and reporting the Brazilian system will require; it matches what CBAM needs.
Keep fuel, reductant and production records per installation.
When a price applies, keep proof of payment and the share attributable to exported goods.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas and electricity invoices and production records into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so the direct emissions behind each tonne can be traced to the documents. Emissions factors outside India are entered from the official source and labelled.
